summary: Full admin regression after the Bewital catalogue import (166 drafts) + new POST /api/admin/products/import/bewital endpoint + freshly-added Bewital one-click UI section. Backend: 20/21 pytest tests pass (the only failure — TestBruteForce — passes on retry; flaky due to per-IP+email identifier where the unique-email subtest gets a fresh bucket each invocation; the lockout logic is correctly wired). All admin CRUD endpoints (products, special-offers, plans, blog-posts, leads, contact-inquiries) return correct status codes and round-trip data. Bewital dry-run (limit=2) returns total_parsed>0 from the API. Public storefront correctly filters out drafts — 0 drafts leak via GET /api/products despite 166 drafts in DB. Frontend: admin login stores JWT in localStorage.SP_ADMIN_TOKEN, dashboard shows live counts (Products 355, Special Offers 0, Leads 12, Contacts 1), products list shows 166 'draft' badges, leads page renders 12 WhatsApp wa.me buttons + CSV export, contact-inquiries page loads. The newly-added Bewital UI section (data-testid='bewital-import-section') and both buttons (bewital-dry-run-button, bewital-import-button) are correctly rendered and clickable. Logout clears localStorage.SP_ADMIN_TOKEN and redirects to /admin/login. ONE non-blocking issue: the UI's 'Preview (dry run)' button returns '502: Request failed' because the import script's dry_run path still calls the Emergent LLM for every one of the ~166 rows (~5+ minutes), exceeding the Cloudflare/k8s ingress ~100s timeout. The pytest dry-run passes only because it uses limit=2. The live 'Run Bewital import' button was NOT clicked (per instructions, to preserve LLM budget).

minor.issue: Dry-run still invokes the LLM for every row (~166 enrichments, ~5+ min) which exceeds Cloudflare ingress ~100s timeout → frontend sees 502. The 'dry_run' flag only skips DB inserts, not LLM enrichment. Either (a) skip enrichment entirely in dry-run and just return parsed-row counts/sample, or (b) expose a 'limit' parameter to the UI for previewing a few rows, or (c) make the route an async background job with status polling.

Brute-force test is flaky in suite runs (passes in isolation). Identifier is IP+email — when X-Forwarded-For from the k8s ingress rotates between hops (or the cleanup interacts with a prior successful admin login in the same suite), the counter may not accumulate. Cosmetic — the lockout logic is correct.

integration_issues.issue: Button triggers a synchronous request that runs the full LLM enrichment over ~166 rows; Cloudflare ingress times out at ~100s and returns 502. End user sees red banner '502: Request failed'. Backend route works for limit=2 (verified via pytest TestBewitalImport::test_dry_run).

action_items: (MEDIUM) Make the Bewital dry-run usable from the UI: either skip LLM enrichment in dry_run (return parsed rows + counts + a few sample previews), OR add a 'limit' input/slider to the UI passed through adminApi.importBewital → backend route, OR convert the route to an async job + polling endpoint.

(LOW) Consider stabilising the brute-force lockout identifier — fall back to email-only when X-Forwarded-For is missing/rotating, or add server-side log of identifier used so flaky tests can be diagnosed quickly.

(INFO) 166 Bewital drafts are correctly hidden from the public /api/products endpoint and visible to admin /api/admin/products list with bilingual EN+KA fields populated. The Bewital partner catalogue spans multiple brands (Belcando 94, Leonardo 47, Bewi Dog 9, 4 Dogs 8, R-Line 4, Bewi Cat 2, etc.) — not all branded literally 'Bewital'. This is expected per the pricelist source.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/admin_routes.py is 813 lines — approaching the 700-line guideline. Consider splitting per-resource (products, special_offers, plans, blog, uploads, leads).

Bewital import route synchronously awaits run_import which makes ~166 LLM calls inside a single HTTP handler. Behind a 100s edge proxy this is guaranteed to 502 on dry-run for the full sheet. Background task + polling pattern is needed for any real one-click UX.

import_bewital_catalogue.run_import treats dry_run only as 'skip DB writes' — enrichment still runs. Decoupling enrichment from persistence (dry_run=True → parse only) would let the UI give the operator instant feedback without LLM cost.
Frontend lib/adminApi.js uses XMLHttpRequest (per intentional Cloudflare workaround) — confirmed working for all admin CRUD/auth/upload calls during this regression.

success_rate.backend: 100% on retry (21/21); 95% on first suite run (20/21, brute-force flaky)
success_rate.frontend: 92% (12/13 review-request UI items pass; Bewital dry-run button returns 502 from ingress)

context_for_next_testing_agent: All admin CRUD verified end-to-end against the public preview URL. The Bewital UI patch (data-testids 'bewital-import-section', 'bewital-dry-run-button', 'bewital-import-button') is present and clickable. ONLY remaining action: main agent should decide if the Bewital UI dry-run UX is acceptable as-is (operator sees 502 after 100s, but the live 'Run Bewital import' actually works because it ran successfully in a prior session — 166 drafts exist), OR refactor dry_run to skip LLM enrichment / background-job the live import. If main agent applies a fix, retest by clicking [data-testid='bewital-dry-run-button'] on /admin/products/import after admin login and confirm a green result panel appears with total_parsed > 0 within 30s.
rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE of Bewital UI 502: POST /api/admin/products/import/bewital?dry_run=true triggers /app/backend/scripts/import_bewital_catalogue.py:run_import which always runs enrich_batch() over every parsed row (calls Emergent LLM ~166 times concurrently). At concurrency=8 this still takes minutes; the Cloudflare/k8s ingress in front of the backend caps HTTP requests at ~100s and returns 502 to the browser. The pytest path uses limit=2 (only 2 LLM calls, completes in <30s) so the backend itself is healthy. REPRO: Login to /admin → /admin/products/import → click [data-testid='bewital-dry-run-button'] → wait ~100s → '502: Request failed' banner appears. MITIGATION (short-term): patch the route or import script so dry_run=True returns immediately with the parsed-row count + bilingual fields for the first N rows (no LLM). Long-term: convert the import to a background task that returns a job_id, with a /api/admin/jobs/{id} polling endpoint.
